components.gap: Source variant not preserved on the reader route. Durrett defines uniform integrability for an arbitrary collection of random variables, with no integrability hypothesis, and derives sup_i E|X_i| <= M+1 < infinity from the definition (PTE5 sec. 4.6, p. 244). def:p15-uniform-integrability (body 15-35) defines the notion only for families of integrable variables. No routed text gives the source's form or shows that uniform integrability of an arbitrary collection forces every member to be integrable: annex 6-7 derives the M+1 bound only inside the integrable setting. The owner's unrouted text supplies it (limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-014.tex body 554-597, annex 480-503), but that text is not on the route.

components.gap: Source variant not preserved on the reader route. Durrett offers Theorem 4.6.2 (PTE5 p. 245) as a common way to check uniform integrability. It takes any function phi >= 0 with phi(x)/x -> infinity and a bound E phi(|X_i|) <= C on a collection with no integrability hypothesis; integrability then follows. thm:p15-ui-moment-criteria (body 48-61, annex 34-74) states the criterion only for a finite Borel Phi and only for families of integrable variables, the setting of def:p15-uniform-integrability. The route nowhere gives the source's arbitrary-phi, no-integrability form or its common-way-to-check claim. Only the owner's unrouted text supplies them (body 599-672, thm:p15-w02c-p15-014-ui-moment-source with the discussion at 622-634; annex 505-549).

components.gap: Justificatory, attributive and evaluative claims inside the cited extent 'thm. 4.6.9 and continuation' (PTE5 pp. 247-248) are absent from the route. These are: the line borrowed from Chung, asking the reader to judge whether Levy's 0-1 law is obvious or incredible; the obvious reading, in which 1_A is F_infinity-measurable and F_n increases to F_infinity, so the best guess of 1_A given F_n should approach the best guess given F_infinity, namely 1_A; and Durrett's evaluation that the tail argument may not show the result to be too unusual or improbable to be possible, though it and later applications show the result is very useful. The route (body 161-176, annex 287-305) gives only the theorem and the incredible reading, the Kolmogorov 0-1 derivation. Only the owner's unrouted text supplies them (body 677-722, def:p15-w02c-p15-014-levy-readings).

The source's name for Theorem 4.6.10 (PTE5 p. 248), 'Dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations', appears nowhere on the route. thm:p15-changing-conditional-limits (body 178-195) is titled 'Changing the variable and the information together' and carries neither that name nor an index entry for it. The mathematics of Theorem 4.6.10 and Exercise 4.6.7 is written with proofs (annex 307-349). Only the owner's unrouted text supplies the name (body 749-775, def:p15-w02c-p15-014-conditional-dominated).

A claim of source Example 4.6.11 (PTE5 p. 248) is omitted. For any uniformly integrable sequence X_n -> X almost surely and any sigma-field F, Theorem 4.6.3 and Exercise 4.6.7 give E(X_n|F) -> E(X|F) in L^1, and the example shows that this cannot be strengthened to almost-sure convergence. Item 3 of thm:p15-ui-counterexamples (body 205-217, annex 368-388) writes the construction and the L^1 convergence of its own B_n, and calls itself 'the complete construction of source Example 4.6.11'. The general L^1 claim, for every uniformly integrable sequence that converges almost surely, is stated neither on the route nor in the owner's unrouted text. It would follow from thm:p15-vitali-convergence together with item 1 of thm:p15-changing-conditional-limits under constant information, but that combination is not written.

Source Exercise 4.6.3 (PTE5 p. 249) ends with a comparative remark: this step-function approximation is much simpler than the bare-hands approach of Exercise 1.4.3, though it uses a lot of machinery. The remark is absent from the route, although body 253 says 'These are the complete source Exercises 4.6.2-3'. The mathematics of Exercises 4.6.2 and 4.6.3 is written (body 229-254, annex 392-456). Only the owner's unrouted text supplies the remark (body 724-747, def:p15-w02c-p15-014-dyadic-price).

The statistical reading and the two definitions of source Exercise 4.6.1 (PTE5 p. 248) are absent from the route. With normal(0,1) Z_i the observations form a sample from a normal population with variance 1 and unknown mean; the distribution of theta is called the prior distribution; and P(theta in . | Y_1,...,Y_n) is called the posterior distribution after n observations. thm:p15-posterior-mean-consistency (body 256-270, annex 458-479) proves the convergence and uses the phrases 'prior variable' and 'posterior consistency', but it defines neither distribution and never identifies E(theta|F_n) as the posterior mean. Only the owner's unrouted text supplies them (body 777-826, def:p15-w02c-p15-014-prior-posterior and thm:p15-w02c-p15-014-posterior-mean; annex 554-589).
